reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: §19.1 gives the professional-and-workmanlike standard plus material conformance to documentation/specifications; §19.2 gives 90 days post-delivery/acceptance for Deliverables and conformance of Hosted Services throughout the subscription term (meeting or exceeding both the 90-day services and 12-month software parameters); §19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law and a no-malicious-code warranty; §19.4 supplies the re-perform/repair/replace-then-refund remedy stack.

Disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty: §19.5 is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and data-protection duties — so no carve-out edit is needed.
No redline and no counterparty comment is the correct output for a compliant finding; the original paragraphs are returned unchanged in the rendered redline.
The failed deterministic check is a phrasing artefact only: the period is spelled out as "ninety days" rather than "90 days", which the regex did not match; the substantive period satisfies the rule.

Rationale accurately flags the only softening (malicious code limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor") and reasonably treats it as market-standard and not worth reopening given the non-exclusive remedies; this does not convert the clause into a deviation under the stated position.
